title: Deployment Governance Authority and Evidence Export Playbook
summary: Playbook for gating customer-facing deployments via a lightweight governance approval that ties RBAC v2 assertions, standardized audit-log schema, automated evidence collection, and SIEM export validation into a single, defensible sign-off process.
overview_notes: Purpose: provide a repeatable checklist and sign-off template for product and infra teams to validate security posture before flipping production traffic. This is intended to be shorter than full pre-launch packages — focused on RBAC v2, audit schema, automation hooks and SIEM ingest readiness. Intended audience: release engineers, security reviewers, SREs and product owners.
deployment_readiness_checklist: RBAC v2 review: confirm all new resources (services, queues, storage buckets) have non-default role bindings and least-privilege policies applied
Role templates: verify roles follow the RBAC v2 naming convention (svc-*, eng-*, secl-*) and include purpose and TTL metadata where applicable

Audit log schema: confirm events for 'authz_grant', 'authz_revoke', 'token_issue', 'token_revoke', 'model_inference_call', and 'data_access' are emitted with the canonical fields: timestamp, actor_id, actor_role, resource, action, outcome, request_id
SIEM mapping: validate field names and types match the SIEM ingest contract (see SIEM mapping snippet below) and run a test payload through the export pipeline

Evidence automation: ensure playbooks that collect signing artifacts (RBAC diffs, policy snapshots, endpoint configs, SIEM ingestion test results) are wired into the release job using the evidence-collector lambda
Backstop and rollback: confirm automated fallback route is configured with lower-tier model or region and that the circuit-breaker policy is annotated in the rollout manifest
Data residency & secrets: verify KMS key usage has a documented key id and key access audit will be exported alongside release evidence
Retention: assert retention windows for audit logs meet regulatory minimums (90d for standard, 365d for regulated customers) and that exported bundles include retention metadata
SLO safety check: confirm latency and error SLOs have no pending overrides that would mask safety regressions
Compliance exceptions: if any exception is requested, attach the approved temporary exception token and the justification document id
signoff_template:
Deployment Governance Sign-off

Deployment: [service-name]
Release window: [start-ISO] to [end-ISO]
Owner (release): [name]
Security reviewer: [name]
SRE on-call: [name]
RBAC v2 status: [pass | minor-findings | major-findings]
Audit schema validation: [pass | fail] (test-run-id: [id])
SIEM export test: [pass | fail] (ingest-run-id: [id])
Evidence bundle location: [gs://or-s3-path]/[bundle-id].zip
Exceptions attached: [yes | no] (if yes list ids)
Final decision: [approve | approve-with-conditions | reject]
Approver signature: [name] [timestamp]
Notes: [free-text]
exception_approval_flow: Submit exception request in Jira component 'sec-exceptions' with tags: rbac-v2, evidence-gap, siem-failure
Security Triage (within 48 hours): assigned security reviewer evaluates risk and assigns temporary TTL for exception up to 7 days or longer with executive approval
Mitigations: require at least one compensating control (e.g., restricted network ACL, additional monitoring rule, or temporary IP allowlist)
Documented rollback plan and owner assigned prior to approval
Approval gating: exceptions >30 days require CISO-level sign-off and a mitigation roadmap in the linked Confluence page
Automation: when an exception is approved, an artifact is generated and stored in evidence bucket and a periodic reminder ticket is auto-created at 75% of TTL
rbac_mappings: role: platform-deployer -> allowed: deploy:start,deploy:rollback,read:config (note: cannot grant other roles)
role: model-ops -> allowed: inference:invoke,cache:flush,metrics:read (scoped to project namespaces)
role: security-audit -> allowed: audit:read,export:siem,exceptions:read (read-only; cannot mutate bindings)
siem_mapping_snippet:
# SIEM Export field mapping (minimal contract)
timestamp -> event.time (ISO8601)
request_id -> event.id (uuid)
actor_id -> user.id
actor_role -> user.role
resource -> resource.name
action -> event.action
outcome -> event.outcome (success|failure)
service -> service.name
region -> cloud.region
additional -> meta.kv (json)

Note: types must be consistent (timestamp string, outcome enum, request_id uuid). Any deviation will be rejected by the SIEM pipeline and produce a 422.
evidence_automation_steps: 1) Release job triggers evidence-collector with list of artifacts: RBAC-diff, policy-snapshots, deploy-manifest, SIEM-test-output
2) Collector runs validators: schema-check, signature-check (GPG/KMS), and retention-tagging
3) On success, collector zips artifacts and writes to evidence bucket with index.json containing summary metadata
4) Collector emits audit event 'evidence_bundle_created' that includes bundle_id and exporter_run_id for traceability
5) If any validator fails, collector posts failure details to the release ticket and auto-creates a blocking task for remediation
retention_and_audit_policy: Audit log retention defaults: 90 days (prod non-sensitive), 365 days (regulated). Evidence bundles retained for 1 year by default. Any deviations require documented exception. All audit exports to SIEM must include retention-policy field and origin-signature hash.
operational_playbook_notes: When performing the governance review, reviewers should: run the SIEM ingest smoke test first (low friction), review RBAC diffs for any wildcard grants, verify evidence bundle integrity, and confirm exception tickets if present are timeboxed. For high-risk services (PII, regulated models) require two independent approvers.
escalation_matrix: Level 0: Release owner (first responder) - triage and small fixes
Level 1: Security reviewer (sec-team) - risk acceptance or short exception
Level 2: SRE lead - infrastructure or rollback decisions
Level 3: CISO or Head of Product - long-term exceptions or regulatory sign-off
examples_and_quick_checks: Quick SIEM smoke: send single sample event with request_id=qa-<timestamp>, expect 200 OK and a matched rule in SIEM within 2 mins
RBAC quick-check: run 'rbac-diff --from=prod --to=release' and ensure zero entries with '*:write' or 'admin:*'
Evidence checksum: run sha256sum on bundle and compare to index.json.signature
